# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to communicate the bomb's visual information to Mute and Blind. Since Blind cannot see gestures or read text, and Mute cannot speak but can hear me and see my gestures, I should speak (which reaches both Mute and Blind) to describe what I see. Mute has the manual and will need this info to guide Blind, but Mute can't speak - only gesture. Blind can hear me directly though.

Let me speak clearly about the bomb's current state so both Mute and Blind receive it.

```
speak(text="Display shows 0. Light is green. Five wires in order: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. Waiting for manual instructions.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute gestured "✌" (two fingers) to me. Since Mute can't speak, this is likely conveying a number or reference - possibly pointing to wire 2, or indicating something has 2 steps, or referring to a rule with number 2. I don't have enough context yet. I should acknowledge and ask for clarification via speech (which Blind can hear too, but this is directed reasoning for Mute who can't hear me back — wait, Mute cannot hear either! Mute can only read and gesture/see gestures? Let me recheck: Mute cannot speak, but can Mute hear? Not stated as unable — only Deaf cannot hear. So Mute CAN hear.

So I can speak to Mute. Let me ask for clarification by speaking, since Mute can hear speech.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see gesture two. Do you mean wire two, the yellow one? Please confirm with gestures - one gesture for yes, two for no.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute gestured "👍" - confirming yes, they mean wire two, the yellow one. This likely means the manual instructs something about wire 2 (yellow). I should relay this to Blind so they know which wire is relevant, since Blind can hear my speech.

```
speak(text="Confirmed: wire two, yellow, is relevant per the manual. Blind, wire two counting from your left is yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]

Mute gestured "👍 ✌" - this could mean confirming yes AND something with two (maybe reinforcing wire 2, or indicating a two-step process, or "yes, cut wire 2" style confirmation). Given the sequence, this seems like agreement plus a repeat of the number two, likely reinforcing that wire 2 is the target action.

I should pass this along and also try to get more detail - perhaps ask if there's an action needed (cut vs leave) since Blind needs actionable instructions, not just identification.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, wire two again. Is the instruction to cut wire two, or to leave it alone? One gesture for cut, two gestures for leave alone.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute gestured "👍" - single gesture, meaning cut wire two (yellow). I should relay this clear instruction to Blind now, since Blind is the one who can actually act on the bomb.

```
speak(text="Instruction confirmed: cut wire two, the yellow wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[CUT] 3:[white] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The wire was cut successfully - the bomb state changed. Now I see new state: display still 0, light changed to blue, wires reordered/changed colors: 1:green, 2:CUT, 3:white, 4:blue, 5:red. I need to report this new state to Mute and Blind so Mute can consult the manual for the next step.

```
speak(text="Success, wire two cut. New state: display shows 0, light is now blue. Wires: 1 green, 2 cut, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:

LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[CUT] 3:[white] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute gestured "☝" - likely indicating wire 1 (green). This suggests the manual now points to wire 1 based on the new light color (blue) or state.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see one finger raised. Do you mean wire one, the green wire?")
wait()
```
